prompt:
You are a hardware-debug illustrator. Draw ONE technical signal-flow diagram (dark background, light labels) explaining a RISC-V RTL failure.
Case: picosoc-uart-div
Failing-trace sha256 (first 16 hex): a7cc571a0a0b3df9
Verbatim diagnosis from the debug agent:
Loopback uart with divider 64 sent 0xa5 but recv returned 0xe0 causing `TRAP: uart data mismatch got 0xe0 want 0xa5` and tohost FAIL 0xdead. Root cause in excerpt is recv bit-period compare uses `(cfg_divider >> 4)` at lines 90 and 97 for data/stop states, sampling ~16x too fast instead of full `cfg_divider`. Via cone picosoc/picosoc.v:190 instance to picosoc/simpleuart.v:20, half-bit align `2*recv_divcnt > cfg_divider` at line 84 is correct, so data bits must use full divider.
Diagram MUST show: the failing signal path named in the diagnosis, the wrong value vs the expected value, and the single RTL line to fix. Annotate the trace hash a7cc571a0a0b3df9 in a corner as provenance. No decorative elements, no invented signals.
